decision: split into 6 children (weighted (floor 4.00 + remainder by contestedness))
Adopt six-branch self-evaluation portfolio with adversary overweighted
why: Six genuinely distinct source bases cover epistemic method, system architecture, reader interface, field failures, evaluation validity, and the strongest disconfirmation; the adversary receives the highest scrutiny because the leading synthesis-interface hypothesis may be an artifact of the requester observations.

decision: Prioritize a lossless-by-reference hierarchical field dossier as the first isolated output experiment; retain the flat bundle only as an inline-transport fallback
why: Observed in checkpoint report.py lines 303-378 and preserved run 2026-07-10-124542: brief.md is 4,606 bytes/72 lines, bundle.md is 950,921 bytes/9,077 lines, and the synthesized brief is appended only after all raw node reads. The code inlines findings/evidence/telemetry/sources/notes but omits decisions.jsonl, questions.jsonl, answers.jsonl, spec.md, and status.json despite calling itself the complete artifact set.

decision: Keep the field-dossier experiment orthogonal to retrieval and accuracy-ledger branches
why: The production baseline and high-accuracy v0.6 work already isolate retrieval, runtime ledger, claim-evidence ledger, dynamic outline, and evaluator mechanisms on separate branches. Mixing them into this reporting experiment would prevent attribution and easy rollback.

decision: Restate sequencing as risk-based project judgment: preserve identity gate experimental; harden whole-answer claim coverage next; test retrieval/reranking third; defer adaptive question graph and stop controller.
why: Fresh-context verification found 29 omitted load-bearing claims, 10 unsupported original rows, and an inconsistent opening/final order; direct wrong-document reproductions made identity a bounded high-severity first implementation while external studies did not compare all workstreams.
